text:
ConocoPhillips rose 0.84% today to $136.12, recovering from a sharp five-day drop that had knocked the stock down nearly 5% from $142.28. The rebound appears tied to escalating tensions in the Middle East: Saudi Arabia and Bahrain reported new attacks involving Iranian-backed forces and Iranian projectiles on November 22nd, which typically tightens oil markets and supports energy company valuations. US crude is trading around $89.50 per barrel, holding steady after the recent slide.

The broader energy backdrop also shifted in the company's favor this week. Senate passage of permitting reform backed by the energy sector on November 20th removes a regulatory hurdle for future projects, while longer-term demand tailwinds—data center electricity consumption potentially doubling by 2030, and Europe facing tight gas supplies heading into winter—suggest sustained pressure on energy supply chains ahead.
